tier_rationale: Manufacturer spec sheet documents the entire control surface as two paddle switches (HIGH/LOW/OFF and PULSE) and lists only electrical ratings (120V, 60Hz, 1560W, 12.5A) with no wireless, app, or programmable-memory feature anywhere in the document. Nothing in the parts and accessories list is a connectivity module.
the_unplug_test: You flip a paddle switch to HIGH, LOW, or PULSE and the motor runs at that setting until you flip it to OFF. There is no memory, no clock, no pairing step, and no vendor server involved at any point between plugging it in and blending. Losing power mid-cycle just stops the motor; there is nothing to reset or re-configure when power returns.

repairability.notes: Manufacturer spec sheet lists a full user-replaceable parts catalog for this model: blending assembly kit, retainer ring kit, drive coupling and coupling-removal tool, plus five container colors and two optional sound enclosures, all sold as standalone SKUs through commercial foodservice distributors.

sources.supports: Manufacturer spec sheet (rev 09/19): paddle-switch controls for HIGH/LOW/OFF/PULSE, 120V/60Hz/1560W/12.5A electrical rating, NSF and ETL/cTUVus certification marks, and a user-replaceable parts list (blade assembly, drive couplings). No wireless, app, or digital-control feature listed anywhere in the two-page document.
Retailer listing corroborating current availability, paddle-switch description, and NSF/UL listing.

open_questions: No FCC search was run since the manufacturer document shows no radio and the device class (a plug-in universal motor with mechanical switches) makes an intentional radiator implausible; worth a cheap confirmatory fccid.io search for the Waring grantee code if this record is ever contested.
notes: Commercial bar/smoothie-shop blender rated for 75 drinks/day. NSF and ETL certification (per PRINCIPLES §3, commercial food-service certifications indicate a product built for an operator who cannot tolerate cloud dependence) plus the full user-serviceable parts catalog corroborate the mechanical-controls read: this is equipment built to be fixed with a wrench, not flashed with firmware.
